y-felinheli.desc: Y Felinheli, on the Menai Straights, Gwynedd, Cymru (Wales). A village and community between Bangor and Caernarfon. Etymologically, its name comes from the Welsh y meaning the, melin meaning mill and heli, meaning brine/salt-water/sea. An alternative interpretation is from Y Felin Heulyn, "the mill on the River Heulyn", which refers to the river that runs into the village.

File:Ysbyty Ifan 440328.jpg
ysbyty-ifan.desc: Ysbyty Ifan, Conwy County, Wales. Looking west towards the village. The warrior monks of the order of St John of Jerusalem, the Knights Hospitaller, had a hospice for travellers at Ysbyty Ifan, founded about 1189. Here they had the privilege of sanctuary for criminals. As the knights lost control of their estates, Ysbyty Ifan became a hide-out for bandits and outlaws.
